findings.description: The statistics dict is now cleared in place and shared by every call, so a re-entrant or overlapping call to the same decorated function resets the statistics of the call still in progress.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a decorated function that calls itself recursively, or is invoked again while an earlier call is still retrying. Mechanism: the inner call runs stats.clear() on the same dict the outer call is writing to, and the outer copy's _local.statistics points at that same dict. The previous code gave each call its own dict, which the comment at this site explicitly preserved. Impact: the outer call's wrapped_f.statistics (for example attempt_number) is reset or overwritten mid-run, so callers read wrong values.

findings.description: The async wrapper clears and reuses one shared statistics dict, so concurrent awaits of the same decorated coroutine write into the same dict.
findings.rationale: Trigger: two asyncio tasks await the same decorated async function at the same time. Mechanism: the second call's stats.clear() wipes the dict the first call is updating, and both copies write to that single dict. Previously each call got a fresh dict, so the calls were isolated. Impact: statistics read through wrapped.statistics for either in-flight call show values belonging to the other call, or reset values.
